entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shaqilath was a queen of the Nabataeans. Her name as transcribed in Arabic is شقيلة Šaqīla.

She ruled from around 9 BC to 40 AD, during which time she expanded her kingdom's borders and established trade relationships with neighboring regions.

As one of the most prominent female leaders of the ancient world, Shaqilath played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and economic landscape of the region. Her reign was marked by significant archaeological discoveries, including the excavation of Petra, which became a major center of commerce and culture.

Despite her importance, Shaqilath's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of her more famous contemporaries, such as King Herod the Great. Nevertheless, her contributions to the region's history remain an essential part of our understanding of ancient Nabataean society.

Shaqilath's impact can still be seen today in the many archaeological sites and artifacts that dot the landscape of Jordan and beyond.
